description: Team Agile is a student-led technology team specializing in AI, Data Science, and software development. We focus on solving real-world problems through innovative, practical solutions. Our team actively participates in hackathons and technology competitions, with achievements including 1st place in Code Air 4.0 and the OpenHome AI Hackathon. We value creativity, teamwork, problem-solving, and continuous learning.
summary: AstroVital is an offline-first health monitoring system for astronauts on long missions, built to answer the challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions”. A custom ESP32 wearable (MAX30102 + DS18B20) streams heart rate, SpO2 and temperature to a Flask backend that scores signal quality and filters noise. An AlertGate escalates to “Get help now” only after 10 consecutive good-quality frames in a rest-verified session, so false alarms stay rare. Personal baselines flag drift, and a readiness score combines heart, bone/muscle and mental checks. MediaPipe Pose counts exercise reps in the browser for a gravity-aware Loading Index (0 g, lunar, Mars), and local Whisper and NLP models assess mood. Dr. NOVA, an OpenHome voice AI doctor, answers from each astronaut’s actual data and comms delay, with an offline fallback. A 3D digital twin, Downlink Report PDF and flight-surgeon Mission Control view support the ground team. It matters because one-way Mars delays of up to about 22 minutes mean crews need a trustworthy first line of care on board. Blood pressure, glucose and respiration are demo-generated
details:
What it does and how it works

AstroVital is an offline-first crew health system for long-duration missions. A custom ESP32 wearable (MAX30102 + DS18B20) samples the PPG signal at 100 Hz, computes heart rate and SpO2 over 4-second windows, detects finger contact, scores signal quality and sends authenticated 1 Hz frames over Wi-Fi. It buffers 5 minutes of data when offline. A Flask backend validates every frame, filters jumps and flatlines, and stores late readings at their true timestamps. Any standard Bluetooth LE heart-rate strap also works through Web Bluetooth.

Configurable YAML thresholds (based on AHA/ACC and ADA ranges) give each metric a status: Good, Okay, Needs attention or Get help now. An AlertGate can only lower a status. Wearable heart rate becomes critical only after 10 consecutive good-quality frames in a rest-verified session. A personal-baseline layer flags drift, and a readiness score combines heart, bone/muscle and mental checks.

MediaPipe Pose runs in the browser and counts reps from joint angles, feeding a Loading Index weighted by gravity (0 g, lunar, Mars). Local faster-whisper and sentiment/emotion models assess mood, behind a regex safety screen. Dr. NOVA, an OpenHome voice agent, answers using each astronaut's actual data and comms delay, with an offline rules engine as a fallback. A 3D digital twin, a Downlink Report PDF and an audited flight-surgeon Mission Control view complete the system.

Benefits and intended impact

Crews get a trustworthy first line of health assessment on board, when Earth is up to 760 s away. Fewer false alarms reduce alarm fatigue. The one-page Downlink Report lets a ground flight surgeon review a crew member quickly over a limited link.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • Hardware: ESP32, MAX30102 pulse oximeter, DS18B20 temperature sensor
  • Firmware: C++ with PlatformIO
  • Backend: Python, Flask, SQLAlchemy, SQLite (WAL mode), pytest
  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js (3D twin)
  • AI: MediaPipe Pose, faster-whisper, Hugging Face RoBERTa models, OpenHome

What is creative

The AlertGate only lowers alerts, which makes false alarms rare. Mission environments change gravity targets, comms delay and advice. The AI doctor is grounded in live data and never invents values. Pose tracking sends only joint coordinates to the server, never video.

Factors we considered

Alarm fatigue, signal noise, privacy, comms delay and offline operation. Mental-health details are hidden from Mission Control. Blood pressure, glucose and respiration are simulated by a physiological model, because no sensor for them is attached.
